tools.name: read_file
tools.title: Read File (Deprecated)
tools.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

tools.name: read_text_file
tools.title: Read Text File
tools.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

tools.name: read_media_file
tools.title: Read Media File
tools.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.title: Read Multiple Files
tools.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

tools.name: write_file
tools.title: Write File
tools.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.title: Edit File
tools.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

tools.name: create_directory
tools.title: Create Directory
tools.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.title: List Directory
tools.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is essential for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: list_directory_with_sizes
tools.title: List Directory with Sizes
tools.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is useful for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

tools.name: directory_tree
tools.title: Directory Tree
tools.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty). The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: move_file
tools.title: Move File
tools.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

tools.name: search_files
tools.title: Search Files
tools.description: Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. The patterns should be glob-style patterns that match paths relative to the working directory. Use pattern like '*.ext' to match files in current directory, and '**/*.ext' to match files in all subdirectories. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.title: Get File Info
tools.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

tools.name: list_allowed_directories
tools.title: List Allowed Directories
tools.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

tools.name: git_add
tools.title: Git Add
tools.description: Stage files for commit. Add file contents to the staging area (index) to prepare for the next commit.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

files.description: Array of file paths to stage (relative to repository root). Use ["."] to stage all changes. Can be omitted when all or update is true.

update.description: Stage only modified and deleted files (skip untracked files).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

staged_changes.description: All staged changes after this operation.

is_clean.description: Whether working directory is clean (ready to commit).

tools.name: git_blame
tools.title: Git Blame
tools.description: Show line-by-line authorship information for a file, displaying who last modified each line and when. For large files, use startLine/endLine to limit output.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

file.description: Path to the file to blame (relative to repository root).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

commitHash.description: Full commit hash of the last change to this line.

author.description: Author who last modified this line.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the commit that last modified this line.

content.description: The actual content/text of this line.

lines.description: Array of blame information for each line.

totalLines.description: Total number of lines in the output.

tools.name: git_branch
tools.title: Git Branch
tools.description: Manage branches: list all branches, show current branch, create a new branch, delete a branch, or rename a branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

newName.description: New branch name for rename operation.

startPoint.description: Starting point (commit/branch) for new branch creation.

force.description: Force the operation, bypassing safety checks.

all.description: For list operation: show both local and remote branches.

remote.description: For list operation: show only remote branches.

merged.description: For list operation: show only branches merged into HEAD (true) or specified commit (string).

anyOf.description: Commit reference: full/short hash, branch name, tag name, or relative ref (HEAD~1).

noMerged.description: For list operation: show only branches not merged into HEAD (true) or specified commit (string).

anyOf.description: Commit reference: full/short hash, branch name, tag name, or relative ref (HEAD~1).

limit.description: For list operation: cap the number of branches returned (applied at the git command). Use on repos with many branches.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

current.description: True if this is the current branch.

commitHash.description: Commit hash the branch points to.

tools.name: git_changelog_analyze
tools.title: Git Changelog Analyze
tools.description: Gather git history context (commits, tags) and structured review instructions to support LLM-driven changelog analysis. Changelog file should be read separately; this tool provides the supporting git data and analysis framework. Pass one or more review types to control what kind of analysis to perform.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

reviewTypes.description: Types of changelog review to perform. At least one required. Options: security, features, storyline, gaps, breaking_changes, quality.

maxCommits.description: Maximum recent commits to fetch for cross-referencing (1-1000).

maxTags.description: Maximum recent tags to fetch for release context (1-1000). Applied at the git command so large tag catalogs do not bloat the response.

sinceTag.description: Only include git history since this tag (e.g., "v1.2.0"). Narrows the analysis window.

branch.description: Branch to analyze (defaults to current branch).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

refs.description: Tags or branches at this commit.

commit.description: Commit hash the tag points to.

gitContext.description: Git history context for changelog cross-referencing.

reviewInstructions.description: Analysis instructions for each requested review type. Guides the LLM on what to look for in the changelog.

tools.name: git_checkout
tools.title: Git Checkout
tools.description: Switch branches or restore working tree files. Can checkout an existing branch, create a new branch, or restore specific files.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

anyOf.description: Branch name (must follow git naming conventions).
Commit reference: full/short hash, branch name, tag name, or relative ref (HEAD~1).

target.description: Branch name, commit hash, or tag to checkout.

createBranch.description: Create a new branch with the specified name.

force.description: Force the operation, bypassing safety checks.

paths.description: Specific file paths to checkout/restore (relative to repository root).

track.description: Set up tracking relationship with remote branch when creating new branch.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

branchCreated.description: True if a new branch was created.

filesModified.description: Files that were modified during checkout.

tools.name: git_cherry_pick
tools.title: Git Cherry-Pick
tools.description: Cherry-pick commits from other branches. Apply specific commits to the current branch without merging entire branches.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

items.description: Commit reference: full/short hash, branch name, tag name, or relative ref (HEAD~1).

mainline.description: For merge commits, specify which parent to follow (1 for first parent, 2 for second, etc.).

strategy.description: Merge strategy to use for cherry-pick.

signoff.description: Add Signed-off-by line to the commit message.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

conflictedFiles.description: Files with conflicts that need resolution.

tools.name: git_clean
tools.title: Git Clean
tools.description: Remove untracked files from the working directory. Requires force flag for safety. Use dry-run to preview files that would be removed.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

force.description: Force the operation, bypassing safety checks.

dryRun.description: Preview the operation without executing it.

directories.description: Remove untracked directories in addition to files.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

filesRemoved.description: List of files that were removed.

directoriesRemoved.description: List of directories that were removed.

dryRun.description: Whether this was a dry-run (preview only).

tools.name: git_clear_working_dir
tools.title: Git Clear Working Directory
tools.description: Clear the session working directory setting. This resets the context without restarting the server. Subsequent git operations will require an explicit path parameter unless git_set_working_dir is called again.

confirm.description: Explicit confirmation required to clear working directory. Accepted values: 'Y', 'y', 'Yes', or 'yes'.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

previousPath.description: The working directory that was cleared (if one was set).

tools.name: git_clone
tools.title: Git Clone
tools.description: Clone a repository from a remote URL to a local path. Supports HTTP/HTTPS and SSH URLs, with optional shallow cloning.

url.description: Remote repository URL to clone from.

localPath.description: Local path where the repository should be cloned.

branch.description: Specific branch to clone (defaults to remote HEAD).

depth.description: Create a shallow clone with history truncated to N commits.

bare.description: Create a bare repository (no working directory).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

remoteUrl.description: The remote URL that was cloned.

localPath.description: Local path where repository was cloned.

branch.description: The branch that was checked out.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.title: Git Commit
tools.description:
Create a new commit with staged changes in the repository. Records a snapshot of the staging area with a commit message.

**Commit Message Format:**
Pass commit messages as JSON string parameters. Multi-line messages are supported using standard JSON string escaping.

**Examples:**
- Single line: { "message": "feat: add user authentication" }
- Multi-line: { "message": "feat: add user authentication\n\nImplemented OAuth2 flow with JWT tokens.\nAdded tests for login and logout." }

Note: Do not use bash heredoc syntax. Literal escape sequences (\n, \t) in the message string are automatically normalized to their actual characters.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

author.description: Override commit author (defaults to git config).

amend.description: Amend the previous commit instead of creating a new one. Use with caution.

allowEmpty.description: Allow creating a commit with no changes.

filesToStage.description: File paths to stage before committing (atomic stage+commit operation).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

commitHash.description: SHA-1 hash of the created commit.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp when the commit was created.

filesChanged.description: Number of files changed in this commit.

committedFiles.description: List of files that were committed.

signed.description: Whether the commit was signed. False when GIT_SIGN_COMMITS=false or when signing was attempted and fell back to unsigned on failure.

signingWarning.description: Populated only when signing was requested but failed, and the commit was created unsigned as a fallback.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.title: Git Diff
tools.description: View differences between commits, branches, or working tree. Shows changes in unified diff format.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

target.description: Target commit/branch to compare against. If not specified, shows unstaged changes in working tree.

source.description: Source commit/branch to compare from. If target is specified but not source, compares target against working tree.

paths.description: Limit diff to specific file paths (relative to repository root).

staged.description: Show diff of staged changes instead of unstaged.

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the diff. Useful for reviewing all upcoming changes.

nameOnly.description: Show only names of changed files, not the diff content.

stat.description: Show diffstat (summary of changes) instead of full diff content.

contextLines.description: Number of context lines to show around changes.

autoExclude.description: Automatically exclude lock files and other generated files (e.g., package-lock.json, yarn.lock, bun.lock, poetry.lock, go.sum) from diff output to reduce context bloat. Set to false if you need to inspect these files.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

diff.description: The diff output in unified diff format.

excludedFiles.description: Files that were automatically excluded from the diff (e.g., lock files). Call again with autoExclude=false to include them.

tools.name: git_fetch
tools.title: Git Fetch
tools.description: Fetch updates from a remote repository. Downloads objects and refs without merging them.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

prune.description: Prune remote-tracking references that no longer exist on remote.

tags.description: Fetch all tags from the remote.

depth.description: Create a shallow clone with history truncated to N commits.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

remote.description: Remote name that was fetched from.

fetchedRefs.description: References that were fetched from the remote.

tools.name: git_init
tools.title: Git Init
tools.description: Initialize a new Git repository at the specified path. Creates a .git directory and sets up the initial branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

initialBranch.description: Name of the initial branch (default: main).

bare.description: Create a bare repository (no working directory).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

path.description: Path where repository was initialized.

isBare.description: Whether this is a bare repository.

tools.name: git_log
tools.title: Git Log
tools.description: View commit history with optional filtering by author, date range, file path, or commit message pattern.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

maxCount.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-1000).

skip.description: Number of items to skip for pagination.

since.description: Show commits more recent than a specific date (ISO 8601 format).

until.description: Show commits older than a specific date (ISO 8601 format).

author.description: Filter commits by author name or email pattern.

grep.description: Filter commits by message pattern (regex supported).

branch.description: Show commits from a specific branch or ref (defaults to current branch).

filePath.description: Show commits that affected a specific file path.

oneline.description: Abbreviated output: return only hash, shortHash, and subject per commit. Significantly reduces response size.

stat.description: Include file change statistics for each commit.

patch.description: Include the full diff patch for each commit.

showSignature.description: Show GPG signature verification information for each commit.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

refs.description: References (branches, tags) pointing to this commit.

stat.description: File change statistics (when stat option is used).

patch.description: Full diff patch (when patch option is used).

totalCount.description: Total number of commits returned (may be limited by maxCount).

note.description: Set when filters returned zero commits. Echoes the criteria and suggests broadening so callers can self-correct without inspecting the request.

tools.name: git_merge
tools.title: Git Merge
tools.description: Merge branches together. Integrates changes from another branch into the current branch with optional merge strategies.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

branch.description: Branch to merge into current branch.

strategy.description: Merge strategy to use (ort, recursive, octopus, ours, subtree).

squash.description: Squash all commits from the branch into a single commit.

abort.description: Abort an in-progress merge that has conflicts.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

conflictedFiles.description: Files with conflicts that need resolution.

tools.name: git_pull
tools.title: Git Pull
tools.description: Pull changes from a remote repository. Fetches and integrates changes into the current branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

rebase.description: Use rebase instead of merge when integrating changes.

fastForwardOnly.description: Fail if can't fast-forward (no merge commit).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

remote.description: Remote name that was pulled from.

conflictedFiles.description: Files with conflicts that need resolution (empty if conflicts is false).

tools.name: git_push
tools.title: Git Push
tools.description: Push changes to a remote repository. Uploads local commits to the remote branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

forceWithLease.description: Safer force push - only succeeds if remote branch is at expected state.

setUpstream.description: Set upstream tracking relationship for the branch.

tags.description: Push all tags to the remote.

dryRun.description: Preview the operation without executing it.

remoteBranch.description: Remote branch name to push to (if different from local branch name).

confirmed.description: Explicit confirmation required for force push or branch deletion on protected branches (main, master, production, etc.).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

remote.description: Remote name that was pushed to.

upstreamSet.description: Whether upstream tracking was set for the branch.

rejectedRefs.description: References that were rejected by the remote.

tools.name: git_rebase
tools.title: Git Rebase
tools.description: Rebase commits onto another branch. Reapplies commits on top of another base tip for a cleaner history.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

upstream.description: Upstream branch to rebase onto (required for start mode).

interactive.description: Interactive rebase (not supported in all providers).

onto.description: Rebase onto different commit than upstream.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

conflictedFiles.description: Files with conflicts that need resolution.

rebasedCommits.description: Number of commits that were rebased.

currentCommit.description: Current commit hash if rebase stopped due to conflict.

tools.name: git_reflog
tools.title: Git Reflog
tools.description: View the reference logs (reflog) to track when branch tips and other references were updated. Useful for recovering lost commits.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

ref.description: Show reflog for specific reference (default: HEAD).

maxCount.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-1000).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

hash.description: Commit hash for this reflog entry.

action.description: Action that caused this reflog entry (commit, checkout, etc.).

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp when this action occurred.

entries.description: Array of reflog entries in reverse chronological order.

tools.name: git_remote
tools.title: Git Remote
tools.description: Manage remote repositories: list remotes, add new remotes, remove remotes, rename remotes, or get/set remote URLs.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

newName.description: New remote name for rename operation.

push.description: Set push URL separately (for set-url operation).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

pushUrl.description: Push URL (may differ from fetch URL).

tools.name: git_reset
tools.title: Git Reset
tools.description: Reset current HEAD to specified state. Can be used to unstage files (soft), discard commits (mixed), or discard all changes (hard).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: Reset mode: soft (keep changes staged), mixed (unstage changes), hard (discard all changes), merge (reset and merge), keep (reset but keep local changes).

target.description: Target commit to reset to (default: HEAD).

paths.description: Specific file paths to reset (leaves HEAD unchanged).

confirmed.description: Explicit confirmation required for hard, merge, and keep reset modes on protected branches (main, master, production, etc.).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

target.description: Commit hash HEAD points to after the reset.

previousCommit.description: Commit hash HEAD pointed to before the reset (omitted if HEAD did not move).

filesReset.description: Files affected by the reset. For path-only resets, the listed paths. For commit-move resets, files that differ between the old and new HEAD. For --hard with no HEAD move, files whose pending working-tree changes were discarded.

tools.name: git_set_working_dir
tools.title: Git Set Working Directory
tools.description: Set the session working directory for all git operations so subsequent calls can omit the path parameter. Always returns a repository snapshot (status, recent commits, recent tags, remotes) to orient the caller.

path.description: Absolute path to the git repository to use as the working directory.

validateGitRepo.description: Validate that the path is a Git repository.

initializeIfNotPresent.description: If not a Git repository, initialize it with 'git init'.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

path.description: The working directory that was set.

repository.description: Best-effort repository snapshot. Omitted when the path is not a git repository (see enrichmentWarnings).

isClean.description: True when the working tree has no changes.

staged.description: Paths staged for the next commit.

upstream.description: Upstream ref being tracked by the current branch.

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

recentCommits.description: Up to 2 most recent commits on the current branch.

date.description: Creator date (ISO 8601); absent for lightweight tags with no metadata.

annotationSubject.description: First line of the tag annotation (annotated tags only).

annotationBody.description: Remaining annotation body after the subject (annotated tags only).

recentTags.description: Up to 2 most recent tags by creator date.

pushUrl.description: Push URL (may differ from fetch URL).

enrichmentWarnings.description: Actionable notes when snapshot gathering was skipped or partially failed.

tools.name: git_show
tools.title: Git Show
tools.description: Show details of a git object (commit, tree, blob, or tag). Displays commit information and the diff of changes introduced.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

object.description: Git object to show (commit hash, branch, tag, tree, or blob).

format.description: Output format for the git object. Use "raw" for unprocessed git output.

stat.description: Show diffstat instead of full diff.

filePath.description: View specific file at a given commit reference. When provided, shows the file content from the specified object.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

content.description: Formatted output showing the object details.

tools.name: git_stash
tools.title: Git Stash
tools.description: Manage stashes: list stashes, save current changes (push), restore changes (pop/apply), or remove stashes (drop/clear).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: The stash operation to perform. Defaults to push (save current changes).

stashRef.description: Stash reference like stash@{0} (for pop/apply/drop operations).

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the stash (for push operation).

keepIndex.description: Don't revert staged changes (for push operation).

limit.description: For list mode: cap the number of stash entries returned (applied at the git command).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

tools.name: git_status
tools.title: Git Status
tools.description: Show the working tree status including staged, unstaged, and untracked files.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the output.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

upstream.description: Upstream ref the current branch is tracking (if any).

isClean.description: True if working directory is clean (no staged, unstaged, or untracked changes). When includeUntracked is false, untracked files are excluded from this check.

stagedChanges.description: Changes that have been staged for the next commit.

unstagedChanges.description: Changes in the working directory that have not been staged.

untrackedFiles.description: Files in the working directory not tracked by git.

conflictedFiles.description: Files with merge conflicts that need resolution.

tools.name: git_tag
tools.title: Git Tag
tools.description: Manage tags: list all tags, create a new tag, or delete a tag. Tags are used to mark specific points in history (releases, milestones).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

commit.description: Commit to tag (default: HEAD for create operation).

message.description: Tag message. Providing a message always produces an annotated tag (git does not support messages on lightweight tags). For release tags, summarize notable changes.

annotated.description: Create an annotated tag with a default "Tag <name>" message. Only effective when no message is provided and signing is disabled — otherwise the tag is always annotated.

force.description: Overwrite an existing tag (create mode only; has no effect on list or delete).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

commit.description: Commit hash the tag points to.

signed.description: Whether the created tag was signed. Only populated for create mode. False when GIT_SIGN_COMMITS=false or when signing failed and fell back to unsigned.

signingWarning.description: Populated only when signing was requested but failed, and the tag was created unsigned as a fallback.

tools.name: git_worktree
tools.title: Git Worktree
tools.description: Manage multiple working trees: list worktrees, add new worktrees for parallel work, remove worktrees, or move worktrees to new locations.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

worktreePath.description: Path for the new worktree (for add/move operations).

branch.description: Branch to checkout in the new worktree (for add operation).

commitish.description: Commit/branch to base the worktree on (for add operation).

force.description: Force operation (for remove operation with uncommitted changes).

newPath.description: New path for the worktree (for move operation).

detach.description: Create worktree with detached HEAD (for add operation).

verbose.description: Provide detailed output for worktree operations.

dryRun.description: Preview the operation without executing it (for prune operation).

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

path.description: Absolute path to the worktree.

head.description: HEAD commit hash in this worktree.

prunable.description: Whether the worktree can be pruned.

tools.name: git_wrapup_instructions
tools.title: Git Wrap-up Instructions
tools.description: Returns a Git wrap-up protocol: an acceptance-criteria checklist the agent must satisfy before the session is considered shipped. Uses the operator's custom instructions if configured, otherwise emits a generic goals-strict/mechanism-generic default. Enriches the response with a repository snapshot (status, recent commits, recent tags) so the agent has immediate orientation for the commit and release steps.

acknowledgement.description: Acknowledgement to initiate the wrap-up workflow.

createTag.description: Controls whether the tag criterion appears in the emitted protocol. Omit or set `true` to include the tag step. Set `false` to omit it entirely — e.g., when tagging is deferred to a separate release step.

instructions.description: The wrap-up protocol to satisfy before the session ships.

repository.description: Best-effort repository snapshot. Omitted when no working directory is set or when the path is not a git repository.

isClean.description: True when the working tree has no changes.

staged.description: Paths staged for the next commit.

upstream.description: Upstream ref being tracked by the current branch.

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

recentCommits.description: Up to 2 most recent commits on the current branch.

date.description: Creator date (ISO 8601); absent for lightweight tags with no metadata.

annotationSubject.description: First line of the tag annotation (annotated tags only).

annotationBody.description: Remaining annotation body after the subject (annotated tags only).

recentTags.description: Up to 2 most recent tags by creator date.

enrichmentWarnings.description: Actionable notes when snapshot gathering was skipped or partially failed.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Close the page

tools.name: browser_resize
tools.description: Resize the browser window

tools.name: browser_console_messages
tools.description: Returns all console messages

level.description: Level of the console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to "info".

all.description: Return all console messages since the beginning of the session, not just since the last navigation. Defaults to false.

filename.description: Filename to save the console messages to. If not provided, messages are returned as text.

tools.name: browser_handle_dialog
tools.description: Handle a dialog

promptText.description: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

filename.description: Filename to save the result to. If not provided, result is returned as text.

tools.name: browser_file_upload
tools.description: Upload one or multiple files

paths.description: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

tools.name: browser_drop
tools.description: Drop files or MIME-typed data onto an element, as if dragged from outside the page. At least one of "paths" or "data" must be provided.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

paths.description: Absolute paths to files to drop onto the element.

data.description: Data to drop, as a map of MIME type to string value (e.g. {"text/plain": "hello", "text/uri-list": "https://example.com"}).

annotations.title: Drop files or data onto an element

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

tools.name: browser_fill_form
tools.description: Fill multiple form fields

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a key on the keyboard

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into editable element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

text.description: Text to type into the element

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL

tools.name: browser_navigate_back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page in the history

tools.name: browser_network_requests
tools.description: Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page. Use browser_network_request with the number to get full details.

static.description: Whether to include successful static resources like images, fonts, scripts, etc. Defaults to false.

filter.description: Only return requests whose URL matches this regexp (e.g. "/api/.*user").

filename.description: Filename to save the network requests to. If not provided, requests are returned as text.

tools.name: browser_network_request
tools.description: Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request, or a single part if `part` is set. Use the number from browser_network_requests.

index.description: 1-based index of the request, as printed by browser_network_requests.

part.description: Return only this part of the request. Omit to return full details.

filename.description: Filename to save the result to. If not provided, output is returned as text.

tools.name: browser_run_code_unsafe
tools.description: Run a Playwright code snippet. Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent.

code.description: A JavaScript function containing Playwright code to execute. It will be invoked with a single argument, page, which you can use for any page interaction. For example: `async (page) => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click(); return await page.title(); }`

filename.description: Load code from the specified file. If both code and filename are provided, code will be ignored.

tools.name: browser_take_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

type.description: Image format for the screenshot. If unset, inferred from the filename extension, otherwise png.

filename.description: File name to save the screenshot to. Defaults to `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg|webp}` if not specified. Prefer relative file names to stay within the output directory.

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

scale.description: Image resolution scale. "css" produces a screenshot sized in CSS pixels (smaller, consistent across devices). "device" produces a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (larger, accounts for the device pixel ratio). Default is css.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

filename.description: Save snapshot to markdown file instead of returning it in the response.

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

boxes.description: Include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in the snapshot. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels (Element.getBoundingClientRect)

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Perform click on a web page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Perform drag and drop between two elements

startElement.description: Human-readable source element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

startTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

endElement.description: Human-readable target element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

endTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Hover over element on page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

tools.name: browser_select_option
tools.description: Select an option in a dropdown

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: List, create, close, or select a browser tab.

index.description: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

url.description: URL to navigate to in the new tab, used for new.

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait for text to appear or disappear or a specified time to pass

time.description: The time to wait in seconds

textGone.description: The text to wait for to disappear
